blocks.x: Security architecture you can evidence — for humans, machines and models. Achala Sentinel is the platform layer behind it — deployed under NDA, documented for the audit.

Achala Sentinel unifies our security delivery: zero-trust enforcement points (identity, posture, segmentation, workload identity), detection-as-code with ATT&CK coverage, cloud posture guardrails, and the AI-specific layer — prompt-injection defense, agent containment, shadow-AI discovery and model security cards. Sentinel is engineered for the evidence economy: controls mapped across SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-207, DORA and AI regimes, tested continuously, exported to auditors. Boards get measured trust reduction, not adjectives.

blocks.x: Sentinel assumes breach and designs for audit: purple-team validation of segmentation, restore-tested backups, AI red-team suites with findings-to-fix tracking. The platform's own controls are SOC 2 Type II audited and ISO 27001 certified.

Achala Sentinel runs under NDA in Banking & Financial Services, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Energy & Utilities, Public Sector & Government, Technology & SaaS. Deployments stay private; the architecture and control packs are the part we can show.
Connects to: SIEM/XDR, SPIFFE/SPIRE, OPA, IdPs/IGA, CNAPP tooling. Adapters are versioned and contract-tested, so upgrades stop being incidents.

Sentinel is privacy-preserving federated learning over a Byzantine-consensus trust fabric. Gradients synchronize over a DAG asynchronously, so latency falls compared with linear sync rounds — and nothing aggregates before a validation unit clears it against accuracy thresholds. Zero-knowledge homomorphic neural encryption keeps each party's data unexposed even during joint computation. Fault monitoring isolates misbehaving nodes and reallocates their tasks without stopping the fleet.

items: Latency drops versus linear synchronization rounds.
Joint computation happens without exposing any party's raw records — including ours.
Accuracy thresholds gate every update; a poisoned gradient never reaches the model.
Cross-party workflows survive untrusted participants by design.
Bad nodes are cut out and their tasks reallocated, mid-flight.
